name: A* Pathfinding
description: A* (A-Star) is an informed search algorithm that finds the shortest path between nodes in a weighted graph. It combines features of uniform-cost search and greedy best-first search, using a heuristic function to guide the search efficiently.
how_it_works: A* maintains two sets: open set (nodes to explore) and closed set (visited nodes). For each node, it calculates f(n) = g(n) + h(n), where g(n) is cost from start, and h(n) is estimated cost to goal (heuristic). It expands the node with lowest f-score, guaranteeing optimality if heuristic is admissible (never overestimates).

complexity.time: O((V + E) log V) with binary heap, worst case O(E)
complexity.space: O(V) for storing open/closed sets and parent pointers

key_parameters: heuristic_function: estimates cost to goal (Manhattan, Euclidean, etc.)
diagonal_movement: allow or penalize diagonal moves
pseudocode_or_diagram_description: Initialize open_set with start node, g[start]=0, f[start]=h(start). While open_set not empty: current = node with lowest f. If current is goal, reconstruct path. For each neighbor: tentative_g = g[current] + cost(current,neighbor). If tentative_g < g[neighbor], update g, f, parent. Add to open_set if not present.
